title: Senior Account Executive - DACH
description: Looking for an innovative, high-growth, multi-award-winning company in one of the hottest segments of the security market? Look no further than Veracode! Learn more at www.veracode.com , on the Veracode blog , and on LinkedIn and Twitter . Own and resolve general sales inquiries pertaining to accounts and respond to RFPs. title: Senior Global Manager, Enterprise Ads & Promos
description: Our Global Structure Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we're unlocking new possibilities as one global team. Senior Global Advertising Manager ​​Join us in our mission to transform the way people shop and eat, where impact, innovation, and growth drive everything we do. Our Advertising team sits at the intersection of commerce, data and marketing helping restaurant and grocery partners accelerate growth through smart, insight-led media solutions. From shaping high-impact campaign strategies to optimising performance at scale, we combine commercial acumen with deep marketplace insight to unlock value for our partners while driving sustainable revenue growth for Deliveroo. We're looking for a Senior Global Advertising Manager to join our London team. This is a hybrid role. In this role, you'll help us craft and execute advertising strategies that exceed the needs of our restaurant partners and drive quarterly growth, both directly with key partners and at scale through enabling and leading global commercial teams. What You'll Be Doing You'll be joining the Ads and Account Management team. We focus on building deep partnerships, enabling commercial teams, and crafting tailored media strategies to accelerate partner growth across our marketplace. Here's what your day-to-day might look like: Identify Data-Led Opportunities: Proactively identify scope to increase advertising penetration and spend using a combination of data analytics and commercial insight. Develop Processes & Go-To-Market Programs: Originating programs and reporting frameworks that organise commercial teams behind key opportunities to track progress effectively. Enable Teams & Build Playbooks: Build playbooks, training, and go-to-market materials that equip global commercial and account management teams to maximise advertising revenue. People & Team Leadership: Manage, coach, and support team members, setting clear goals and fostering a culture of high performance and professional growth. Partner Strategy & Campaign Management: Work directly with major restaurant partners to understand marketing objectives, propose tailored ad solutions, and coordinate campaign launches, management, and reporting. Performance Monitoring & Optimisation: Proactively monitor campaign performance, identifying, communicating, and resolving any issues to exceed partner objectives. Shape Product Solutions: Act as the voice of our partners to feed structured feedback back into internal teams, informing how we iterate and build improved advertising and reporting products. What You'll Need to Thrive Essential Commercial Advertising Experience: Significant experience in commercially focused roles, with a strong background in performance advertising or account management. People Leadership & Management: Proven ability to manage, coach, and develop team members, driving high engagement and performance against commercial targets. Strategy & Process Scaling: Demonstrated capability in defining, launching, and scaling go-to-market strategies and operational processes across teams. Stakeholder Management: Exceptional relationship-building skills with a proven ability to work effectively and build trusted relationships with multiple internal and external partners. Analytical & Innovative Thinking: Highly analytical mindset with strong capability to interpret data and turn findings into strategic commercial recommendations. Nice to Have Digital Marketing & Marketplace Experience: Prior exposure to digital marketing environments, e-commerce, or aggregator platforms. Why Join Us? At Deliveroo, you'll do work that matters, solving real-world problems in a three-sided marketplace that's constantly evolving. We're food lovers, problem solvers, community builders and more, brought together by a shared drive to make things better. Working here you can expect to: 🔧 Make a visible impact every day Your work directly improves experiences for customers, partners and riders. 🌱 Learn fast in an entrepreneurial environment Work close to the market with autonomy, pace and real responsibility. 🧠 Build a career, not just a role Stretch yourself, develop new skills and grow as the business evolves. 🌎 Deliver together in an inclusive culture Collaborative, values-driven teams that support how you work best. We aim to create a fair process that lets your skills shine—our interview typically includes 3-4 stages. Find more about how we hire here. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across Do orDash and Wolt. Together, we're unlocking new possibilities as one global team. Diversity, Equity and Inclusion At Deliveroo, we know that a great workplace reflects the world around us and that true diversity and inclusion make us stronger, more creative, and better at what we do. We're committed to fostering an environment where everyone can do their best work and feel they belong. Coca-Cola, LinkedIn, Adobe, LVMH and Bayer are just a few of the 2,400+ global companies who rely on our best-in-class platform.</p> <p style="padding-left: 40px;"> Our Winning Culture is the engine that drives our teams of innovators. We champion diversity of thought and ideas, we behave like leaders regardless of title, we are committed to achieving ambitious goals, and we love celebrating<em> </em>our wins – big and small.</p> <p>Supported by operating principles of being strategy-led, <a href="https://www.anaplan.com/careers/">values-</a>based and disciplined in execution, you’ll be inspired, connected, developed and rewarded here. Everything that makes you unique is welcome; join us and let’s build what’s next - together!</p></div><p>Anaplan is seeking a <strong>Solution Architect</strong> to join our <strong>Professional Services team in the UK</strong>—a group of expert consultants who are passionate about delivering real, measurable value through Anaplan’s cutting-edge planning platform.</p> <p>As a key member of our Professional Services team, you won’t just be implementing solutions, you’ll shape the future of enterprise planning for our most strategic customers. title: Clinical AI Research Lead
description: We’re Heidi. We're building the future of healthcare by giving every clinician the earth's finest AI Care Partner. Our platform has absorbed the administrative chaos of 175 million patient visits and supported 67 million clinical hours. Today, we support 2.8 million patient sessions a week across 190+ countries, in 110 languages and over 200 specialties. Healthcare systems are failing us; clinicians spend more time on documentation than on patients, and the human connection that makes medicine worth practicing is eroding. Our mission is simple: double the world’s capacity for care and strengthen the human connection at its heart. We found product-market fit with a freemium medical scribe that clinicians love. Now, we're expanding. Every task a clinician hands to Heidi is a patient who feels more attended to, a health system unclogged, and a clinician who gets to be a clinician again. We’ve grown annual recurring revenue from $1 million to $50 million in two years. To go further, we’ve secured US$340 million: a $100 million Series C led by Blackbird, with Phoenix Court, Point72 Private Investments and Headline, alongside a $240 million growth investment led by General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund. If you want to join us in doing work worth shipping, jump in. The role Heidi is building AI that works at the frontier of clinical practice. As we pursue medical device registration and expand our clinical trial portfolio and product portfolio, we need someone who can hold the full arc from regulatory strategy to research protocol to working prototypes and translate across all of them. This role is designed for a rare profile: clinically trained, technically capable, and research-rigorous. You will own the innovation pipeline from problem identification through validated prototype, coordinate the company's clinical research programme, and serve as the internal bridge between product, regulation, and evidence. You will operate as a senior individual contributor with a small specialist team and broad cross-functional mandate. What you’ll do Research & Evidence Programme Lead and support clinical trials and pilots adjacent to product development and regulation from protocol through analysis and dissemination Design evaluations with research/publication-grade rigour: statistical power, confounder control, reproducible methodology Provide analytical support company-wide - elevating ad hoc analysis to defensible evidence Regulatory & Compliance Intelligence Translate evolving UK and international medical device regulation into actionable product and development constraints Generate and maintain technical documentation, clinical evaluation reports, and post-market surveillance artefacts - directly analytically supporting the regulatory team. Partner with compliance to ensure regulatory soundness is built in, not bolted on, a strategic moat, not a checklist Serve as the accessible regulatory resource for product, engineering, models and commercial teams: making regulation legible, usable and deeply embedded into all engineering practices. This role is strategic support, and ownership of all product and regulatory adjacent research activities with a strong supporting team to drive progress and delivery. Cross-functional AI & Research Support Act as a senior research partner to product squads, commercial teams, and leadership, providing evidence, framing decisions, and raising analytical standards Supporting commercial requests with tender applications etc… What you'll need Clinical Qualified clinician with active understanding of clinical workflow, risk, and patient safety Experience in medical device or clinical AI evaluation, including familiarity with MHRA, UKCA, and/or EU MDR frameworks Research Postgraduate research training in a relevant field (clinical informatics, AI/ML, health data science, or similar) Demonstrated ability to design, execute, and disseminate clinical or applied research independently Fluency in quantitative methods: statistical modelling, NLP evaluation, speech analytics, and performance benchmarking Skills in implementation science and translational projects involving new technologies Leadership & Communication Strong written communication, capable of producing high-quality documentation for clinical, regulatory, and commercial audiences Collaborative operator in a fast-moving environment; able to work across seniority levels and functions Experience managing small teams or contractors; structured, outcome-oriented How we show up Build for the next decade, not next quarter . Our targets are outrageous on purpose. The world's health doesn't have the luxury of incrementalism. Lead, don't wait . We treat tomorrow's problems today. Sometimes we build what's needed before it's wanted, and we're fine with that. Follow the evidence . Trust the patient. We pursue truth relentlessly. But when the subjective and objective disagree, we treat the patient, not the numbers. Ego is a comorbidity we can't afford. Own the outcome . Everyone here carries the company. Raise problems with solutions, solve them end-to-end, and never be a bystander. Ship, measure, go again . A button today, a workflow tomorrow. More iterations beat better planning. We're precise at pace, not reckless. Live in clinicians' reality . Not the ideal workflow, the twenty-patients-before-lunch actual one. We build for exhausted humans, and we'd better be decent ones while we do it. Why Heidi? You’ll join a team measured on real-world impact, not press cycles. We live and breathe the challenges of modern health systems, and are laser-focused on exacting the change we’d like to see. We’re medicos, engineers, builders and designers who’ve felt (on every side of the equation) what non-care feels like, the moral and practical toll as a provider or receiver. Building what we’re building isn’t always easy. Standard tech playbooks routinely fail in healthcare, and the friction of the medical system will test your perseverance. But we didn’t choose easy, we chose a purpose-driven mission that actually matters. We hold ourselves to a higher standard because healthcare demands it. If you join Heidi, you recognize that the deeper question isn’t whether AI can solve the global healthcare crisis, but whose hands will shape it. True A-players progress extremely fast here. The nature of the scale-up game is demanding, but we value sustainable performance and mental health. You're trusted to perform, and you set your schedule. We operate on outcomes > inputs, not process theatre. We all take the bins out, metaphorically and literally. We take care of you. We offer 25 days of paid time off per year, 24/7 mental health, coaching and wellbeing support through Sonder, a €100/month Healthy Heidi's wellness stipend, a €500 home office budget, a €700 annual learning and development budget, 26 weeks paid primary parental leave and 18 weeks paid secondary parental leave, fertility support up to €7,000, up to four weeks of work from anywhere per year, Recharge Days after major milestones and busy periods, 10 days per year of clinical leave for eligible clinical roles, and a hybrid working environment with 3 days in the office. We chose to open-source our benefits hub , if you care to take a peek. Heidi’s commitment to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Heidi is dedicated to creating an equitable, inclusive, and supportive work environment that brings people together from diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. Our strength is in our differences. We're proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are proud to welcome all applicants as we're committed to promoting a culture of opportunity for all. title: Site Reliability Engineer
description: At Signal AI, we use cutting-edge AI technology to offer clarity on decisions that shape businesses and society. We value restless curiosity, creative thinking, and diverse perspectives as we strive to become AI-native. We believe that AI is a collaborator, not just a tool, and we invite passionate individuals to join us on our journey as we continue to learn, experiment, and grow together. We're hiring a Senior SRE to help us run and evolve the infrastructure behind Signal AI's decision intelligence platform. You'd be joining a small, collaborative Infrastructure team at a moment when the work is genuinely changing shape. Over the last year, we've hardened the platform, reduced cost, and built serious observability into our highest-volume systems. The next year is about scaling that work, absorbing infrastructure from a recent acquisition, and being thoughtful about how AI shows up in operational work: not as a gimmick, but as a tool we trust ourselves to use well. We're looking for someone who wants to shape the team's direction; someone people can rely on for tricky or urgent problems; someone who brings curiosity and care to the work; and someone who wants to leave things meaningfully better than they found them. What we've shipped recently Cut ~$50k/year off our Elasticsearch bill by migrating compute to more efficient chips. (Apr 2026) Built the foundation for our MCP server platform : leveraging and contributing to open-source tooling to give the whole company extensible, production-grade AI integrations. (2025–2026) Rebuilt production from scratch in a full DR game day . End-to-end restore validated across our multi-account AWS setup. (Jan 2026) What we're working on next AI-augmented operations : Claude Enterprise is deployed across Signal. We want this team to help define what good looks like for SRE: incident triage, runbook generation, capacity planning, cost analysis. This is a strategic investment, not a side project, and we'd love someone genuinely curious about what these tools can and can't do. Security in the age of AI : The threat landscape has shifted. Supply chain security is more at threat than ever, and powerful models are emerging that promise to change how the industry thinks about security. We're looking for someone interested in thinking seriously about what actually matters to protect now. Acquisition integration : Bringing a recently acquired product's infrastructure under our reliability, security, and operational standards. A substantial, multi-quarter piece of work with real technical and organisational complexity, and plenty of room to make your mark. Batch workload consolidation : Moving disparate batch jobs onto EKS for unified scheduling, cost visibility, and operational tooling. Your first six months We want to set you up to thrive. Here's what that looks like in practice: Month 1 : You're onboarded across our AWS estate, Terraform, and observability stack. title: Applied AI - Member of Technical Staff
description: About Us We’re living through a Cambrian explosion of intelligence: new models and new chips, each specialised for different tasks, are arriving all at once. The result is a new era for AI, one of radical heterogeneity. Callosum is the Intelligent Systems Company. We believe the next generation of AI won't be defined by any single model or chip, but by intelligent systems in which hardware and intelligence co-evolve. We are building the infrastructure that unifies heterogeneous compute across the full stack. This opens a new axis of scaling intelligence: a dynamic system that tailors itself to what each workload actually needs, whether that's speed, cost, precision, or whatever unit comes next. The last era scaled on a different bet: one bigger model, more of the same chip, more data. That bet is running into structural limits. Frontier models offer extraordinary capability at unsustainable cost, one that today's monolithic infrastructure was never designed to serve. Our founding principle is that intelligence comes from many specialised systems working together, not from any single component. We build the software orchestration layer that co-evolves models, workflows and silicon into one system, delivering inference tailored to every workload, and demonstrating orders-of-magnitude leaps in capability and cost. Because our software spans the full stack, our engineering team works directly with heterogeneous accelerators and frontier silicon, including Cerebras, d-Matrix, Intel, NVIDIA, AMD, Normal Computing, Tenstorrent, GreatSky, and Mixx. We are not stopping at today's chips: each new generation of silicon unlocks algorithms that couldn't run before, and we intend to be first to them, every time. If we get it right, it will belong to everyone building on it - not to any single vendor. In our latest funding round, we raised $100M, led by Atomico with participation from Plural, DCVC and the UK Sovereign AI Fund’s first investment. With this, we are building the infrastructure for the next era of intelligence. We are engineers and scientists based in London, working across the full depth of the stack. We are curious, intellectually honest, and building what doesn't exist yet. If you thrive on uncharted territory and are energised by the scale of the challenge, we'd love to hear from you. About the Role Applied AI Research at Callosum discovers the methods that make real AI workloads faster, cheaper and better, and turns them into systems that run in production. You will study how agentic workflows, retrieval pipelines and code intelligence stacks actually behave, then invent ways to optimise them at a systems level. A single optimisation can touch agent and workflow design, context and prompting, model choice, the serving stack and the silicon underneath. So we don't hire specialists in one layer. We hire researchers who can reason across the whole system, from agentic design down to the specifics of the model, and who have a feel for how inference and hardware shape what is possible. The role is research-led and engineering-heavy. You will need first-principles judgment to see what kind of system a problem needs, the rigour to prove that it works, and the engineering skill to build it yourself. You will sit across our research and platform functions. What you discover becomes product capability, and what you see in real workloads sets the research agenda. We run a flat Member of Technical Staff structure. Responsibility and scope grow with what you demonstrate, including leadership of the Applied AI Research function as the team scales. What You'll Work On Our research tries to construct optimal inference systems from the silicon layer all the way up to the harness: the system will learn from the actual deployment profile and tasks it is used on and optimise itself. Open problems you will own include: •⁠ ⁠ Reverse-engineering agentic systems. Infer the structure of agentic systems from minimal data, and find where it spends compute it doesn't need to. •⁠ ⁠ Routing. Build robust routers that send each request to the cheapest or fastest path that strictly matches or beats the incumbent model on quality. •⁠ ⁠ Proving there is no regression. Design layered proxy evaluations, that bound quality ever more tightly, from coarse checks down to a granular understanding of the system. •⁠ ⁠ New optimisation surface area. Extend the same automatic, detection to new optimisation techniques, and help decide which ones we pursue next. •⁠ ⁠ Research that ships. Run rigorous experiments, write up what you learn, and work with our platform team to turn what works into general product capability. •⁠ ⁠ Shared research infrastructure. Build the evaluation harnesses, benchmarks and experiment tooling the team runs on. How We Work •⁠ ⁠ Generalists by design. Our cadence is fast and our priorities move as we learn. You will move between projects as the problem demands, so breadth and the speed at which you learn matter more than depth in one niche. •⁠ ⁠ Research judged by production. A result counts when it holds on real workloads. Ideas move quickly from hypothesis to experiment to a deployed system. •⁠ ⁠ Close to real workloads. You work from real production systems and pipelines. Customer contact is scoped: team members who show an aptitude for it can take on more customer-facing technical work, but it is not the core of the role. •⁠ ⁠ A mix of experience. We hire across seniority levels. Experienced researchers bring proven practice from large-scale AI development, earlier-career members bring speed and fresh eyes, and each learns from the other. What You Bring •⁠ ⁠Broad, foundational knowledge across the modern AI stack: agent and workflow design, LLMs and how they work inside, and inference and serving. You can reason about how a change in one layer affects the others. •⁠ ⁠Exceptional technical depth, demonstrated through any of: research that shipped, production AI systems at scale, or an early or founding role where you owned the system end to end. •⁠ ⁠Rigour in experimental design, evaluation and benchmarking. You can tell a real improvement from noise, and you design the measurement before you trust the result. •⁠ ⁠A very fast learner who goes to first principles when the map runs out. •⁠ ⁠Strong engineering skills: you build the systems you research. •⁠ ⁠A bias for action, comfort with ambiguity and a strong sense of ownership. What Sets You Apart •⁠ ⁠An early or founding role at an AI-first, deep-tech company, where you made key technical decisions from first principles. •⁠ ⁠You have designed and built multi-agent or agentic systems from the ground up, and you also have depth lower in the stack. •⁠ ⁠Low-level systems or performance engineering: kernels, serving engines or latency-critical systems. •⁠ ⁠Experience of large-scale AI development at a frontier lab or big tech company, and the engineering practices that come with it. •⁠ ⁠Research in inference optimisation, model internals, evaluation, routing or distillation. •⁠ ⁠Publications, open-source work or public write-ups that show how you think. •⁠ ⁠Familiarity with novel accelerator platforms. •⁠ ⁠Experience working directly with external engineering teams. What We Offer •⁠ ⁠Competitive Salary, determined by skills and experience •⁠ ⁠Equity & Ownership •⁠ ⁠Private healthcare •⁠ ⁠We offer Visa sponsorship and relocation benefits to hire the best in the world •⁠ ⁠We work in person at our London office. You'll have the tools, space and setup to do your best work, and if you have specific needs, just tell us We're committed to building an inclusive workplace where everyone feels welcome, and believe in equal opportunities for all. title: Senior Global Brand Manager
description: About Us Avenir Collective. Building the future of beauty, personal care and lifestyle brands. We acquire and scale high-potential consumer brands, bringing together the capital, people and operating expertise to turn strong brands into enduring businesses. Our difference is that we are operators, actively managing our brands and providing the capabilities, infrastructure and expertise they need to scale, while preserving the product, purpose and consumer connection that make each brand special. We’re building a connected house of brands where great people, brands and ideas come together. If you’re excited by building businesses, solving problems and working with a collaborative, entrepreneurial team, we’d love to hear from you. Your role at a Glance We are looking for an entrepreneurial, commercially grounded Senior Global Brand Manager to take ownership of two of our most exciting growth opportunities: a male grooming brand and a skin health brand. Both have built strong foundations as digital-first, Amazon-led businesses, with proven products and loyal customers. The next chapter is about turning them into true omnichannel brands, with clear positioning, distinctive identities and sustainable growth across key markets. Reporting to our Chief Brand Officer, you will be the senior brand lead across both categories, setting direction and rolling up your sleeves in equal measure. Initially you will work largely hands-on, partnering closely with product, creative, digital commerce and commercial colleagues to land key priorities. As you prove the model and build the case for further investment, you will have the opportunity to shape and grow a team around you. This is a role for someone who loves building: someone who takes ownership, moves at pace, brings people with them and gets things done. The Mission Both brands are at an inflection point. They have earned their place online through great products and performance-led growth, but their brand foundations have not yet caught up with their ambition. Positioning, identity and the wider brand ecosystem now need to evolve so that each brand can travel beyond a single marketplace, win in new channels and with retail partners, and stand for something clear in the mind of the consumer. The task at hand: I n male grooming, evolve and sharpen the brand so it builds on a strong core proposition and grows into a broader, more relevant grooming brand for today’s man. In skin health, build credibility and trust in a category where efficacy and reassurance matter most, creating a brand that consumers and retail partners can believe in. Across both, translate brand strategy into omnichannel go-to-market plans that land in market, across retail, direct-to-consumers and marketplaces beyond Amazon. Deliver early, visible wins that demonstrate commercial impact and build the business case for future investment in the brands and the team . Location and Flexibility Full-time role based at our modern office in Runway East, London 40 hours per week, 9 am to 6 pm with a one-hour lunch This position is hybrid, with the expectation to go to the office 2 days per week Key Responsibilities Brand Strategy & Portfolio Leadership Own the global brand strategy, positioning and identity for both the male grooming and skin health brands, ensuring each is clear, distinctive and relevant across markets. Lead brand evolution work, from consumer insight and positioning through to visual identity, packaging and tone of voice, moving the brands from marketplace-led to brand-led. Build annual brand plans with clear growth targets, KPIs and investment cases, and take accountability for delivery against them. Put the consumer at the heart of every decision, using insight, data and real-world understanding to shape messaging, product experience and activation. Track category trends, competitor activity and emerging opportunities in grooming and skin health and turn them into action. Develop brand guidelines, playbooks and toolkits that make it easy for teams, partners and markets to bring the brands to life consistently. Brand Activation & Commercial Delivery Partner with product, creative, digital commerce and marketplace commercial teams to develop and land go-to-market plans at pace. Lead omnichannel campaigns across e-commerce, retail, social media, PR, influencer and community platforms. Bring a “glocal” mindset: consistent global brands, with room for smart local adaptation. Work hand in hand with the commercial team on retailer sell-in, providing compelling brand stories, decks and assets, and joining key customer conversations where needed. Manage and get the best from external agency partners across creative, PR, social and digital, within agreed budgets. Measure performance rigorously, connecting brand activity to commercial outcomes and adjusting course quickly . Leadership, Collaboration & Building for the Future Build strong, trusted relationships across the business and with external partners, bringing people with you through influence rather than authority. Act as a trusted advisor to senior leadership on brand opportunities, risks and growth priorities. Build the case for future investment in the brands and in brand capability, using results and insight to show what is possible. Experience & Capabilities Significant brand management experience, with a track record at senior manager level or equivalent, in male grooming, skin health, personal care, beauty or adjacent consumer health categories. Proven experience building, repositioning or evolving brands, including positioning, identity, packaging and messaging. Experience taking brands beyond a single channel, ideally from digital or marketplace-led into retail and wider omnichannel. Strong commercial grounding: confident with P&Ls, retailer dynamics, pricing and business cases, and able to link brand investment to commercial returns. Experience leading campaigns and brand activation across multiple markets. Strong creative judgement and a good understanding of digital, social and content trends. Excellent agency management and stakeholder management skills. Experience in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial, or scale-up environment is highly desirable. Benefits Salary: £60,000 - £70,000 30 days holiday + 8 UK bank holidays Pension contribution Scheme – 5% from you, 3% from us. Private Medical Insurance – Includes travel, vision & dental (Vitality) Work from Abroad – One month per year, anywhere in the world Bonus Scheme – Discretionary bonus, based on individual and company performance Mental Health Support – Free, confidential therapy via Spill Flexi-Fridays – Finish early one Friday per month Avenir Events – Quarterly meetups, celebrations & socials Vibrant Office – Runway East, Bloomsbury This is a rare opportunity to take two beauty and personal care opportunities to the next level, driving momentum and shaping their future while laying the foundations for a team and a truly brand-led business. You will have genuine ownership, senior visibility and the autonomy to make a tangible impact from day one . Note: By submitting your application to join our talent pool, you consent to the collection and processing of your personal data in accordance with our privacy policy. title: Lead AI Security Engineer - Remote (UK Only)
description: A platform you can believe in: Immersive One is the leading cyber resilience solution across the globe. Could you be our next AI Security Engineer? Due to customer demand and increasing maturity within our platform, we have an exciting and challenging opportunity for an experienced, innovative, data-driven Cyber Security Engineer with a background in implementing security in AI products to join our Container 7 team as a Lead AI Security Engineer. We’re looking for someone with a builder mindset who enjoys creating, improving, and scaling ways of working. You’ll have full ownership and accountability for your area, with real scope to shape the role and make it your own. You’ll thrive in a small team with a broad remit, where there is plenty of opportunity to learn, develop, and grow alongside the business. As a Lead AI Security Engineer, you will be a key player in our Container 7 team, shaping and influencing the rollout of our AI & Cyber security roadmap, simulating attack paths, demonstrating how to secure infrastructure and build security into your agents and AI landscape from day one - all while helping train our users to counter the latest threats. You will be constantly researching, learning, totally geeking out on all things AI security-related, from agentic security to the latest AI-driven attacks, and then taking that knowledge and creating labs and ranges for our customers. This role would suit someone who is immersed in the AI security field and has strong insight and opinions on how our product roadmap should evolve to ensure our customers have the tools to learn how to build and deploy AI securely You will design, build, and deliver practical and theoretical content to gamify AI security and make it engaging and fun for the end user. You'll shake up traditional training and teach complex concepts in an innovative way. If you have an extensive background in cyber security - in particular AppSec and cloud security - are experienced in the area of securing AI agents and securing AI-driven platforms, and want to disrupt how employees build their resilience against the latest threats, we will appreciate your input and give you the space to innovate within our market-leading platform, Immersive One, and our new AI Security product. Your main responsibilities: Utilising knowledge of offensive & defensive appsec and cloud security engagements to plan, write and deploy AI security labs, challenges and online learning content on the Immersive One platform. Lead on the building of content around security vulnerabilities in AI and Large Language Model (LLM) deployments (e.g., prompt injection, data poisoning, model evasion). This could be multi-format content utilising various teaching methods; practical exercises, questions & gamification Test AI Security labs and ranges to ensure they function as expected Research vulnerabilities, tools, and offensive tactics and compile this research to deliver practical and theory labs to users Compile technical research into understandable, concise content for both technical and non-technical audiences Work with the wider Product team on new projects and product innovations and how best to deploy them Sounds good? We’d love to hear from you if you have proven experience in the following areas (we know it’s tough, but please try to avoid the confidence gap. You don’t have to match all the listed requirements exactly to be considered for this role): Proven and extensive experience in application security, product security, or cloud security, with a strong focus on AI/ML or LLM technologies. It would be highly desirable if you are experienced in threat modeling for LLM and agent systems, agent permission design, Guardrails and output validation, evaluation and regression testing, model drift detection, and Drift prevention Thought leader within AI Security - you’re someone who is constantly reading the latest whitepapers and thinking several sprints ahead as to what we should be building within our AI Security product roadmap. Excellent communication skills to partner and build relationships with engineering and product colleagues outside of the core security team. You’re a self-starter who is comfortable working with autonomy, takes initiative, and spots opportunities to add value. You bring a hands-on approach, with a willingness to get stuck in and support across a broad range of priorities when needed. Deep understanding of the AI threat landscape, including the OWASP Gen AI Security Project and MITRE ATLAS, as well as an understanding of adversarial machine learning techniques. You possess strong attention to detail, have a logical approach to problem-solving, and the ability to multitask in a fast-paced environment. Hold strong programming skills (e.g., Python) and familiarity with common AI/ML frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow, LangChain). Immersive’s growth has been fuelled by our values that underpin everything we do, here's how they relate to this role: Driven - We push the boundaries of innovation, acting swiftly to achieve ambitious outcomes. Our drive embodies a culture of ambition, where challenges are stepping stones to excellence. Inclusive - Our strength lies in diversity, fostering a culture where every individual contributes to our collective strength. We champion open dialogue and empathy, ensuring a collaborative, inclusive workplace. Customer Centric - We seek to develop deep relationships with our customers to help them achieve their business outcomes. We exceed our customers and partners' expectations by crafting products, services and experiences that surprise, delight and ensure they feel valued and supported every day. One Team - We are a talented global team working together to achieve our vision. Central to our ethos, resilience means adapting and thriving in adversity. It guides our innovation, ensuring we and our clients are prepared for the future. We encourage people of all different backgrounds and identities to apply. We are committed to maintaining an inclusive, supportive place for you to be you and do your very best work. Excited by the above? We’re ready to receive your application! As well as an inclusive, supportive place for you to be you. We offer an extensive range of benefits so you can do your very best work: Time off, flexible and remote working so you can work when is best for you, includes 25 days annual leave + 2 volunteering days and your birthday off. The longer you are with Immersive, the more holiday days you get, up to a maximum of 30 days after five years of service. Look after your family and yourself with enhanced parental leave, mindfulness groups, critical illness cover, 7% matched pension, private healthcare plan and more. Career and learning development through the platform, a dedicated professional development fund and our ‘Learn Anything’ fund - which enables you to learn anything that’s not work! Recognition & Rewards for doing great work and living our values and behaviours. Informal or formal flexible working options, e.g. flexible start and finish times, reduced hours. We have a vibrant team culture with team events throughout the year. Our socials have included everything from pottery painting and paper mask making, to dungeons and dragons! title: Customer Care Student Support
description: Summary We're looking for a Customer Care Student Support who wants to help UK pet parents mainly during evenings and weekends, alongside their studies. You'll be a direct line between Lassie and the people trusting us with their pet's health: answering questions over chat, email and phone, and making sure every conversation leaves them feeling looked after. Lassie is the opposite: the go-to platform for managing every part of pet parenthood - health, insurance, payments, products, services and community - built around the pet and the people who love them. We've raised $75M in Series C, we're live in Sweden, Germany, France and the UK, and we're just getting started. As a fast-growing scale-up, we hold ourselves to a high bar when it comes to our work: real ownership, fast execution, and decisions made like the business depends on them, because it does. Three values shape how we work: Speed Machine - we move fast while others hesitate Packed with Passion - we care deeply about our work and the pet parents we do it for Copied Since 2021 - we don't follow trends, we create them. We look for people who already work this way: people who care deeply, deliver fast, and want to help set the standard the rest of the industry ends up following. What we're looking for Available to work a minimum of 10-20 hours per week, covering our core hours: 8.00am–8.00pm Monday to Sundays Excellent written and spoken English, and comfortable switching between chat, email and phone A warm, patient communicator who stays calm and clear when a pet parent is worried or frustrated Curious and structured - you notice patterns in what customers ask and want to make things better You take ownership without waiting to be told. You see what needs fixing and you fix it Bonus: Previous experience in customer service or pet related field like a vet clinic. It is also important that you’re someone who Love pets of course! title: Senior Researcher, Human Rights and Artificial Intelligence
description: <p><strong>FULL-TIME JOB VACANCY</strong><br><strong>Senior Researcher on Human Rights and Artificial Intelligence</strong><br><strong>Technology, Rights and Investigations Division</strong><br><strong>Multiple Office Locations Considered</strong><br><strong>Application Deadline: December 13, 2026</strong><br> <br>Human Rights Watch (HRW) is seeking a highly qualified Senior Researcher on Human Rights and Artificial Intelligence to investigate, analyze, and advocate against human rights abuses worldwide related to artificial intelligence. The role of the Senior Researcher will include documenting and conveying the rights implications of various forms of artificial intelligence and other algorithmic decision-making being developed and deployed by governments and private sector actors around the world for exclusion and repression, including  information control and censorship and discriminatory decision making, especially in high-risk contexts, for example by law enforcement and immigration authorities. Experience working on the impact of AI or other technology issues in Asia is preferred.</p> <p>The role sits in the Tech and Human Rights team within the broader Technology, Rights and Investigations Division and will report to the Deputy Director based in New York. The Senior Researcher on Human Rights and Artificial Intelligence will collaborate with other team members in the Technology, Rights and Investigations Division, and colleagues in regional and thematic divisions, and other relevant departments of HRW, including media, legal and policy team, and the advocacy department.</p> <p>The successful candidate will have deep domain expertise, as well as a track record of conducting research and investigations at the intersection of human rights abuses and AI. The role will be based in any of the following locations where HRW has an office, and will be expected to work from the office on an as-needed basis: New York, Washington DC, Los Angeles, San Francisco, Toronto, Sao Paulo, London, Brussels, Amsterdam, Berlin, Nairobi, Johannesburg, Beirut, or Stockholm. </p> <p><span style="text-decoration: underline;"><strong>Responsibilities:</strong></span><br>1. Develop a plan for strategic research and advocacy for influencing the development, application, and regulation of artificial intelligence and similar technologies by governments and the private sector to ensure respect for internationally recognized human rights, including non-discrimination and accountability;<br>2. Research, document, and analyze policies and practices related to AI, machine learning, and big data technologies that raise human rights concerns by collecting and analyzing information from a wide variety of sources, including governments, media, academia, NGOs, victims of abuses, open-source information, technologists, and others; Interview persons whose rights have been harmed by AI technologies, as well as related professionals and experts (e.g., organizations representing impacted communities, engineers who build AI technologies, data and computer scientists, etc.); <br>3. Identify and document where use of AI may have disparate impact on vulnerable or marginalized groups or may exacerbate economic inequality, and place abuses or potential for abuses within the broader political, social and economic contexts;<br>4. Write and publicize reports, op-eds, press releases, briefing memos, statements, testimony and other materials to disseminate our research findings and policy recommendations for preventing or ending human rights abuses linked to artificial intelligence applications; <br>5. Work with colleagues in the Communications Department to develop innovative multimedia and social media strategies to communicate our positions in clear and compelling ways and to advance advocacy;<br>6. Develop and implement advocacy strategies in collaboration with HRW colleagues to change or prevent abusive government laws, policies, and practices, as well as abusive corporate policies and practices; <br>7. Press companies and governments to ensure human rights protections are built into artificial intelligence by design from the outset and articulate how existing human rights standards should apply to emerging AI technologies;  <br>8. Build partnerships across key communities, including other human rights NGOs, groups representing vulnerable populations, data scientists, machine learning programmers, tech industry leaders, and academics; <br>9. Contribute to the shaping of public debates on AI around human rights internationally through clear and prompt responses to queries from policy makers, the media, colleagues, and human rights communities; <br>10. Work collaboratively with an international team of researchers within the Technology, Rights and Investigations division, including the Digital Investigations Lab, other thematic and country HRW researchers, and other relevant departments of HRW, including Communications, Legal and Policy, Advocacy, and the General Counsel’s office;<br>11. Travel domestically and internationally, as required, to conduct research, media work and advocacy; and<br>12. Be prepared and willing to work flexible hours to accommodate developing and urgent events;<br>13. Carry out other tasks as required.</p> <p><span style="text-decoration: underline;"><strong>Candidate Profile </strong></span></p> <p>Candidates who are traditionally underrepresented in the technology and/or human rights sectors (such as people who identify as BIPOC, LGBTQIA+, women, migrants, people with disabilities, or people who have other related lived experiences) are enthusiastically encouraged to apply if they feel they have the ability to succeed in this role, even if they do not have all the skills and qualifications listed below.</p> <p><strong>Education:</strong> An advanced degree in journalism, law, public policy, national security, computer science, or a related field or equivalent experience is required.</p> <p><strong>Experience:</strong> A minimum of seven years of experience is required. This experience could come from a<br>variety of previous roles including, but not limited to journalists who have covered technology,<br>community activism, work at impact litigation organizations, academics, or industry professionals.</p> <p><strong>Related Skills and Knowledge</strong>:<br>1. Extensive knowledge of artificial intelligence, in particular the threats and complexities it poses to the major human rights challenges of our time is required.<br>2. Experience working on the impact of AI or other technology issues in Asia and fluency in an Asian language are desirable. <br>3. Strong commitment to understanding how technology can impact the rights of women, racial and ethnic minorities, children, older people, people with disabilities, people living in poverty and low-wage workers, and other populations whose rights may be disproportionately impacted by AI is desirable.<br>4. Proven track record of producing timely and high-quality written research and investigations, as well as editing experience is required.<br>5. Ability to present and defend complex technology-related issues and positions to officials in governments, companies, and other bodies and institutions is preferable.<br>6. Being comfortable with generating and executing research projects, and the curiosity and creativity to follow through and follow up is required.<br>7. Exceptionally strong research, analytical, writing, and editing skills are required.<br>8. Experience conducting challenging investigative research globally is required, as is the ability to dig deep and tenacity in finding hard-to-get information, sources and records.<br>9. Good oral and written communication skills in English, and strong public speaking skills, are required; proficiency in other languages, is highly desirable.<br>10. Experience with TV, radio, print, and social media is highly desirable.<br>11. Demonstrated ability to work independently as well as successfully with a team and across other teams is required.<br>12. Strong interpersonal skills to work collaboratively within HRW, as well as develop constructive relationships with NGO partners, and company and government officials are required.<br>13. Demonstrated awareness and sensitivity to the needs and concerns of individuals from diverse cultures, backgrounds, and orientations is required.</p> <p><span style="text-decoration: underline;"><strong>Salary and Benefits</strong></span>: HRW offers competitive compensation and employer-paid benefits. HRW offers relocation assistance package and will assist employees in obtaining necessary work authorization in all listed locations except Nairobi, if required; citizens of all nationalities are encouraged to apply. If based in the United States, the salary range would be 88,000 – 104,000. Salary ranges outside of the United States vary based on location.<br> <br><span style="text-decoration: underline;"><strong>How to Apply</strong></span>: Please apply by December 13, 2026, by visiting our online job portal at careers.hrw.org and submitting a cover letter and CV or resume. No calls or email inquiries, please. Only complete applications will be reviewed and only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. <br> <br>If you are experiencing technical difficulties with your application submission, or if you require disability-related accommodation, please email ----- Rights Watch is strong because it is diverse</strong>. We actively seek a diverse applicant pool and encourage candidates of all backgrounds to apply. Human Rights Watch does not discriminate on the basis of disability, age, gender identity and expression, national origin, race and ethnicity, religious beliefs, sexual orientation, or criminal record. We welcome all kinds of diversity. Our employees include people who are parents and nonparents, the self-taught and university educated, and from a wide span of socio-economic backgrounds and perspectives on the world. Human Rights Watch is an equal opportunity employer. </em><br><em> </em><br><em><strong>Human Rights Watch </strong>is an international human rights monitoring and advocacy organization known for its in-depth investigations, its incisive and timely reporting, its innovative and high-profile advocacy campaigns, and its success in changing the human rights-related policies and practices of influential governments and international institutions. </em></p> Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Customer Success Leader, Enterprise Law Firms, Northern Europe
description: Why Harvey At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come. This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched. Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you. At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started. Role Overview As Customer Success Leader, you lead the team that is custodian of value for Harvey's Enterprise law-firm customers across Northern Europe. You own gross and net revenue retention across the segment, built on Harvey becoming embedded in how each firm's practice groups work and every firm moving along the AI maturity curve. You will be a visible executive presence with managing partners and firm leadership across a portfolio of prestigious, high-profile firms. Prove value : coach your team to align each firm on measurable outcomes — capacity, realisation, matter economics, client impact — and capture the value stories and ROI evidence that underpin renewal and growth. Lead at partner level : grow CSMs into trusted advisers who cultivate champions and partner sponsors, and engage directly with managing partners, senior partners and innovation leaders at the segment's key firms. Set the standard for the firm's journey : define and scale the playbooks — mutual success plans tied to each firm's objectives, kickoffs, implementation reviews, QBRs and executive business reviews — that take every firm from pilot to daily use, practice group by practice group. Orchestrate cross-functionally : partner with Sales, Legal Engineering, Innovation Partners, the Transformation Office and Product leaders so each firm gets the right expertise at the right moment. Run the product feedback flywheel : turn the voice of law-firm customers into prioritised input for Product and Engineering, and into improvements in how we deliver. What You Have Ideal candidates for the Customer Success Leader, Enterprise Law Firms role at Harvey can demonstrate comfort and experience with the following: A proven background leading high-performing Customer Success or account management teams in late-stage or post-IPO enterprise SaaS, serving strategic or lighthouse accounts with substantial six-figure annual spend — ideally law firms or other professional services firms. A track record of owning and delivering a team-level revenue, retention or net-revenue-retention number, with accurate forecasting. Building teams through hiring, coaching and developing talent, with a leadership style grounded in empathy and a high bar. Designing and scaling playbooks that take enterprise customers from initial adoption to embedded, organisation-wide use, with measurable outcomes grounded in concrete use cases. Building multi-threaded relationships at senior level and influencing partners and stakeholders who did not buy the product. Portfolio planning and revenue-based prioritisation across a regional book, including early identification and mitigation of risk. Quantifying and communicating business value and ROI to senior legal stakeholders. An AI-native way of working: you use AI and sophisticated tooling daily, can show how it has changed your own and your team's output, and have a point of view on how AI changes legal practice. Communicating and influencing at every level, internally and externally, including running in-person meetings with managing partners and firm leadership. With built-in governance, auditability, and human oversight, Camunda gives enterprises the control they need to move AI from pilots to production — safely and at scale. Trusted by over 700 organizations worldwide , including 9 of top 10 US banks, Camunda helps enterprises boost operational efficiency, accelerate time-to-value, and deliver better customer experiences. Fully remote and global, we are in the middle of something bigger: transforming into an AI-first organisation, built on our own platform . We use Agentic AI to automate, orchestrate intelligent processes, and elevate human contribution across every team. Named GP Bullhound’s Top 100 Next Unicorn list, 2025 Great Place to Work certified. Visionary in 2025 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Business Orchestration and Automation Technologies. ranked 3rd in Flexa's 2026 Most Flexible Companies , We’re growing fast and looking for top talent to join our team. This role builds and runs the engine behind that partner business: the program, the investments, the data, and the operating rhythm. The Principal Program Manager is the strategic operating partner to the VP of Partnerships & Alliances and leads an AI-first approach to how the partner team works. title: Music Community Ambassador | First Chair Programme
description: Help shape the future of music teaching in London Are you part of London’s music community and passionate about teaching? Join First Chair , Matchspace Music’s founding ambassador programme, and help bring Europe’s leading platform for music educators to musicians across London. We’re selecting six musicians to help launch Matchspace Music in the UK. You’ll connect with fellow musicians across the city, share what you’re hearing on the ground, and help us understand what independent music teachers need to build and grow their teaching practice. You won’t be handed a script to promote. You’ll help shape how we arrive in London, from the very first week. About Matchspace Music Matchspace Music is Europe’s leading platform for music educators. We help independent music teachers build a professional online presence, get discovered by students, manage their lesson offers and get paid, all in one place. Founded in Switzerland in 2020, we are home to more than 2,000 qualified teachers across over 100 instruments, with more than 2,100 international teachers registered ahead of our launch. We’re now bringing this to the UK, starting with London. What you’ll do As a First Chair ambassador, you’ll: Introduce Matchspace Music to musicians in your peer networks. Start conversations about teaching and the challenges of building an independent teaching practice. Share feedback from your community with the Matchspace Music team. Contribute your own perspective to help shape our UK launch. Work with the team to develop an approach that feels relevant and authentic to London’s music community. This is a six-month freelance engagement, working remotely for four hours per week , starting immediately. Hours can be planned around your studies or other commitments. What you’ll bring We’d like to hear from musicians who: Are actively connected to London’s music community. Care about music teaching and want to help improve how it works. Enjoy meeting people and feel comfortable starting conversations. Can share thoughtful, constructive feedback. Want to help shape how we launch in London. Can commit four hours per week for six months. A student or recent graduate of a London conservatoire, we’re starting conversations at RAM, RCM, Guildhall and Trinity Laban, and welcome ambitious musicians from across the city, in any discipline: strings, piano, voice, jazz, composition and beyond. What you’ll get Paid participation: £25 per hour. Flexible scheduling around your studies or other commitments. Direct access to the founder and opportunities to contribute to product discussions. A voice in the UK launch , helping us understand and respond to musicians’ needs. Lasting recognition as a founding ambassador. A dedicated contact: Fanny Chelle, musician, teacher and Customer Success Specialist, who will welcome you and guide you through the programme. Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Sr Product Manager II
description: <div class="content-intro"><h4><strong>Join Axon and be a Force for Good.</strong></h4> <p>At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Like our products, we work better together. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other.<br><br>Life at Axon is fast-paced, challenging and meaningful. Here, you’ll take ownership and drive real change. Constantly grow as you work hard for a mission that matters at a company where you matter.</p></div><p>Axon's mission is simple and bold: <strong>Protect Life.</strong></p> <p>We build technology that helps first responders, security teams and communities act with speed, clarity and confidence in the moments that matter most. Our Real-Time Operations (RTO) portfolio, anchored by the Fusus platform, is transforming how law enforcement, enterprise security and international agencies detect, assess and respond to threats.</p> <p>Fusus connects live video, alerts, sensors and location data into a unified operating picture, and the map is where that picture comes together. It shows where every officer, vehicle, camera, drone and sensor is, what state it is in, and what is happening around it. We're building a map that stays clear under pressure, so operators and responders can see what matters and act in seconds.</p> <h3>Your Impact</h3> <p>As Senior Product Manager for Maps & Presence, you will define and lead the roadmap for how Fusus shows the world in real time. You'll own the live map, floor plans and the presence layer: the "dots on the map" that tell operators who and what is where, and whether that information is fresh.</p> <p>You'll own the map experience operators use every shift and the map services every other team builds on. Your work will let any device, sensor or data source appear on the map in a consistent way, without bespoke work for each one. That spans body cameras, fleet vehicles, drones, CCTV, sensors and third-party devices, indoors and outdoors.</p> <p>You'll also lead the map in Axon's next generation of Fusus: role-based experiences built from shared components, where every role gets a map designed for its job. Your work will help responders find the nearest resource, follow an incident as it moves and reconstruct what happened afterwards, directly advancing Axon's mission to Protect Life.</p> <p><strong>Work Location: </strong>This role is based out of our London office and follows a hybrid schedule. We rely on in-person collaboration and ask that team members work onsite Tuesdays through Fridays, with the flexibility to work remotely on Mondays, unless there is an approved workplace accommodation. We believe that connection fuels innovation, and our in-office culture is designed to foster meaningful teamwork, mentorship, and shared success.</p> <h3>What You'll Do</h3> <ul> <li>Own the Maps & Presence product roadmap, focused on a map that is clear, consistent and fast to act from</li> <li>Define one behavior model for every real-time dot on the map (how each device type looks, clusters, shows state and freshness) and retire legacy formats</li> <li>Own the map services and contracts (layers, geo-boundaries, floor plans, the Presence API) that let other teams put new data on the map through self-service</li> <li>Build self-service floor plans and map layers for customer admins, so setup no longer depends on Support or Professional Services</li> <li>Lead the map and floor-plan components for Fusus's role-based experiences, shipping them in today's Fusus first</li> <li>Deliver location history (breadcrumbs) and cross-camera tracking for investigations, with Search and video teams</li> <li>Partner with engineering and design to ship responsive, low-latency and reliable map experiences across web and mobile</li> <li>Engage law enforcement and enterprise users in real-time crime centers and the field to validate needs and test improvements</li> <li>Use metrics and feedback to set priorities: dot freshness, map load time, presence coverage, time from alert to action</li> <li>Support go-to-market, training and rollout with cross-functional teams</li> </ul> <h3>What Success Looks Like</h3> <ul> <li>Operators trust what they see on the map: every device looks and behaves the same way, and stale data is obvious</li> <li>New devices and data sources appear on the map in days, without map-team engineering work</li> <li>Customers set up their own floor plans and layers, and filter the map to what matters to them</li> <li>Adoption grows across customer segments with high daily use, strong retention and positive field feedback</li> <li>Every second saved contributes to safer outcomes for officers, teams and the public</li> </ul> <h3>What You Bring</h3> <ul> <li>6–8+ years of product management experience, including 3+ years on map-based, location or real-time products</li> <li>Experience building products where speed, clarity and reliability directly affect outcomes</li> <li>Strong grasp of geospatial and presence concepts: map rendering and clustering, layers and tiles, geofences, indoor mapping, location data quality and freshness</li> <li>Familiarity with live video, sensor networks, fleet or asset tracking, drones and IoT integrations</li> <li>Experience with platform products that other teams build on, including APIs and data contracts</li> <li>Track record of turning user insight into clear product direction and focused execution</li> <li>Proven ability to lead cross-functional teams through roadmap, design, delivery and iteration</li> <li>Clear communicator who drives alignment, decisions and measurable outcomes</li> </ul> <h3>Why Axon</h3> <ul> <li>Shape the future of how responders and security teams see and act on the world around them, creating safer outcomes for communities and organisations</li> <li>Join a mission-driven company with a history of innovation and impact</li> <li>Work alongside passionate teams building technology that protects lives</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Benefits that Benefit You</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Competitive base salary and RSUs</li> <li>Pension plan with matching contributions</li> <li>Private health insurance and cash plans</li> <li>30 days paid holiday plus UK public holidays</li> <li>Enhanced maternity and paternity leave</li> <li>GymPass subscription</li> <li>Life assurance and income protection</li> <li>Career growth, learning support, and wellness resources</li> </ul> <p> </p><div class="content-conclusion"><p>Don’t meet every single requirement? That's ok. At Axon, we Aim Far. We think big with a long-term view because we want to reinvent the world to be a safer, better place. We are also committed to building diverse teams that reflect the communities we serve.</p> <p>Studies have shown that women and people of color are less likely to apply to jobs unless they check every box in the job description. If you’re excited about this role and our mission to Protect Life but your experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification listed here, we encourage you to apply anyways. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.</p> <p><strong>Important Notes</strong></p> <p><em>The above job description is not intended as, nor should it be construed as, exhaustive of all duties, responsibilities, skills, efforts, or working conditions associated with this job. title: Biomedical Scientist
description: Mission Neko Health is a health technology company that opened its first clinic in Stockholm in 2018, founded by Daniel Ek and Hjalmar Nilsonne. In one hour, our scan combines radiation-free imaging, heart and circulation measurements, and same-visit blood results with time to talk it through with a clinician, so people can act on what matters before symptoms appear. We design and build our own hardware, software and clinical protocols, and more than 100,000 members have already had a scan, with 75% booking and prepaying their next one before they leave. As a team, we chase 10X, not 10%, and we’re looking for people who think the same way to help us scale what we’ve started in Sweden, the UK, and now the US. Join the clinicians, engineers and business builders making prevention a routine part of care. Role Purpose This is not a traditional laboratory role. We're looking for a Biomedical Scientist who is comfortable working differently, embraces innovation, and takes pride in delivering accurate results at exceptional pace. Neko Health members come through our clinics for whole-body preventive health screenings, and our laboratories sit at the centre of the patient journey. They are busy, modern spaces, and the service continues to develop as we scale. This is a hands-on, autonomous role, based on site in one of our central London laboratories. As a Biomedical Scientist, you will operate our Abbott Alinity and Sysmex XN-550 analysers and support the quality systems that allow us to return results within 30 minutes of sample receipt. If you're a BMS looking to further develop your career in an innovation-led environment, we would love to hear from you. What You'll Deliver in the First 6 - 12 Months Initialise the analysers each day and ready them for sample processing. Perform testing on our Abbott Alinity (biochemistry and immunoassay) and Sysmex XN-550 (haematology) analysers, validating patient results and escalating clinically anomalous or unexpected findings. Carry out daily calibration, internal quality control, and routine maintenance of analysers, troubleshooting and escalating technical issues promptly. Work within our ISO 15189-aligned, UKAS-facing quality management system: author SOP updates, monitor EQA performance, support audits, and investigate non-conformances. Contribute to service improvement work, including analyser verification, reagent evaluation, and software testing. Maintain accurate, auditable records and support performance monitoring across turnaround times, KPIs, and consumables usage. Provide technical guidance to clinical colleagues and support training across the lab team. Minimum Requirements HCPC registration as a Biomedical Scientist, with evidence of ongoing CPD. Minimum one year of post-registration experience in clinical chemistry and immunoassay, including IQC and EQA practice. Demonstrable experience operating an integrated clinical chemistry and immunoassay analyser. Experience working accurately and efficiently under time pressure, suited to a low-volume, fast-turnaround service model. Preferred Post-registration experience in haematology. Hands-on experience operating Sysmex XN-series haematology analysers. Hands-on experience operating Abbott Alinity ci-series. Experience in POCT, rapid diagnostics, or high-throughput clinical settings. Experience with laboratory information management systems (LIMS), digital result reporting, or involvement in LIMS development and user acceptance testing. title: Area Medical Lead, North & Midlands
description: Mission Neko Health is a health technology company that opened its first clinic in Stockholm in 2018, founded by Daniel Ek and Hjalmar Nilsonne. In one hour, our scan combines radiation-free imaging, heart and circulation measurements, and same-visit blood results with time to talk it through with a clinician, so people can act on what matters before symptoms appear. We design and build our own hardware, software and clinical protocols, and more than 100,000 members have already had a scan, with 75% booking and prepaying their next one before they leave. As a team, we chase 10X, not 10%, and we’re looking for people who think the same way to help us scale what we’ve started in Sweden, the UK, and now the US. Join the clinicians, engineers and business builders making prevention a routine part of care. Role Purpose You own the clinical bar across the Neko clinics in the North and Midlands (currently Birmingham and Manchester). That means every consultation in your area meets the same threshold of safety, quality, and member experience across your region. It means the clinical teams working with you are developing, not just performing. It means clinical issues are being seen and addressed before they show up in audits or member complaints. And it means the quality metrics for your region are known, owned and moving in the right direction. And it means clinical judgment shows up at the table when operational decisions are being made. You'll partner closely with the UK Medical Director, who holds final clinical authority for the UK market, and operate in true dyad partnership with the Area Clinic Manager for your region who owns the operational side. The clinical health of the region is yours. What You'll Deliver in the First 6–12 Months Hold the clinical standard across every site in your area Manage and develop the clinicians in your region: performance conversations, development plans, coaching, and the honest feedback that turns good clinicians into great ones. Ensure lead clinicians in your market(s) are performing excellently and that the clinical teams have the appropriate clinical escalation pathways in place. Support clinical hiring for your area against defined criteria, and partner with the Training and Education team to close training gaps as they emerge. Own the review and closure of clinical incidents and near-misses in your area, making sure learnings are actually applied, not just documented. Own the quality metrics for your region: accountable for performance against Neko's medical quality goals at area level, including scan quality (perfect scan score), member follow-up quality and timeliness (perfect follow-up score and follow-up SLAs), clinical safety (Northstar Clinical Safety score) and clinician summary quality and timeliness. Review the data with your Area Clinic Manager each week and month, trace variation to root cause by site and clinician, set improvement actions, and report progress and risks to the UK Medical Director. Operate in true dyad partnership with the Area Clinic Manager: co-owning quality, member experience, and business goals, attending and contributing to Weekly and Monthly Business Reviews, and bringing clinical input into operational decisions before they're made. Round your sites regularly to observe, support, and listen, surfacing what's working so it can spread, and what isn't so it can be addressed. Build and maintain trusted relationships with the GPs, NHS trusts and private specialist clinicians who receive Neko referrals, monitoring referral quality and addressing breakdowns quickly. Know the UK regulatory landscape: CQC registration and inspection standards, GMC/NMC professional standards and revalidation, NHS and GP referral pathways and obligations, and UK-specific clinical rules, and flag emerging risks before they become problems. Lead or participate in clinical pilots as required - defining success, capturing learnings, and documenting outcomes so the rest of the company can learn from your region. What We're Hiring For Holds the Bar at Scale. You're the kind of clinical leader who can make sure every consultation feels the same regardless of site or clinician, not by micromanaging, but by setting a clear standard, coaching to it, and noticing when it drifts. You're rigorous without being rigid. Develops the Clinicians You Lead. You take clinician development seriously. You give honest feedback even when it's uncomfortable. You spot what someone needs before they ask. You know the difference between a clinician who needs coaching and one who needs to leave, and you don't avoid either conversation. The Dyad That Actually Works. You bring clinical judgment into operational decisions before they're made and you stay constructive when clinical standards and operational targets pull in different directions. When you escalate, it's because something genuinely needs leadership attention, not because you've stopped trying to resolve it locally. Reads the Pattern, Not Just the Report. You don't just review the data. You see what it's telling you. You round your sites and notice things that don't show up in dashboards. When you spot a pattern you trace it to the root cause and you make sure the right people hear about it. Trusted Outside the Walls. The referral network, the regulators, the specialist clinicians who receive Neko members: these relationships sit with you. You represent Neko credibly because you're a credible clinician yourself. People in the local medical community know your name, and when you flag something, they take it seriously. Minimum Requirements Full GMC registration with a license to practice, in good standing and with a current revalidation, and right to work in the UK. On the GMC GP Register with qualification (CCT or equivalent) in General Practice. 4+ years of medical leadership experience in the UK health system (NHS and/or private sector), including direct management of clinicians. Demonstrated experience holding clinical standards across multiple sites or a large clinical team. Preferred Experience in preventive care, tech enabled healthcare or longitudinal care models. Experience operating in a clinical-operational dyad structure. Experience leading clinical pilots or scaling new clinical workflows across multiple sites.
